content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices, especially in early periods, indicating a lag in capturing true market dynamics.", "Sentiment spikes often precede sharp price corrections, suggesting sentiment can trigger mean-reversion in carbon markets.", "Model forecasts show minimal variance in early days but diverge sharply from true outcomes after 10–15 days, signaling diminishing predictive power.", "High sentiment positivity correlates with forecast overshoots, implying sentiment amplifies model bias rather than corrects it.", "True outcomes frequently exhibit volatility spikes after 10-day horizons, suggesting models fail to anticipate sudden regulatory or market shocks.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, indicating models are more reliable under subdued market sentiment.", "Models exhibit persistent upward bias in early forecasts, suggesting a structural overconfidence in price appreciation.", "Sentiment history should be weighted more heavily in model calibration to reduce forecast drift and improve alignment with true market behavior."]}
